newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly down.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Friday, with many investors staying on the sidelines, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,196 yuan ($385) per tonne, rising six yuan. It opened at 3,196 and hit a low of 3,195.
March fell one to 3,237, May 20 to 3,330, July 10 to 3,340, September 20 to 3,360 and November was unchanged at 3,400.
Combined volume fell to 15,959 tonnes from 17,000.
Traders said many investors did not want to build new positions ahead of the weekend, which resulted in slow trading.
"Long liquidation by retail investors dominated today's trade, with the short-term market trend unclear," one trader said. "Few investors wanted to hold positions over the two-day holiday," he added.
Traders said soybean would consolidate around 3,200 yuan in the next few trading days due to a lack of market-moving news.
